P-boom readout 1 (8 receipts, 19,200 evaluations each, 600 archived generations; preregistered statistic = spikes >= 2/16 in reward_max per 100 archived generations). A_baseline s1/s2/s3: 0.17 / 2.83 / 5.67; B_shuffle s1/s2/s3: 1.67 / 3.00 / 3.33; C_no_coupling: 5.67; F_popcapture_s1: 5.17. Within-arm spread (0.17 .. 5.67 in A) exceeds the between-arm difference by an order of magnitude. INSTRUMENT FACT: A_baseline_s1 and F_popcapture_s1 were specified as the same world, seed and evaluation order and differ from generation 1 (1 vs 31 spikes); reproduced exactly from the receipts with nomination removed: the segment folded run_id (= experiment_id) into the c6.segment, wse.eval and c6.plant streams, so every arm of v1 ran on an independent random stream. The v1 'same seed, one thing changes' premise was false; v1 arms are valid as independent-stream data only.

No reading of order vs population is possible until arms share their streams (v2, K_ arms, stream_key). Rulers population_shift/max_spike remain AUTHORITY NONE.
